TITLE: BETTOR public-research architecture audit
GENERATED_BY: offline reading of public literature against the BETTOR code as committed
PROMOTION_RULE: No entry may move to production without BETTOR-NATIVE out-of-sample evidence beating the named benchmark. A paper is a reason to TEST, never a reason to ADOPT a number.
SAFEGUARDS_THAT_MAY_NOT_BE_WEAKENED: PROVENANCE: DISPATCH_SHA == EXECUTED_SHA_ACTUAL, four aspects, schema versions
THREE_VALUED_UNCERTAINTY: NOT_IDENTIFIED never evaluates to zero
CENSORING: interval- and right-censored observations stay censored
FILL_IDENTIFICATION: a touch is never a fill; MoveThroughIsNotAFill raises
INCENTIVE_SEPARATION: TRADING_NET_EX_INCENTIVES reported before any total
REENTRY: PROHIBITED_REENTRY_MOTIVES, size independent of sunk P&L
NO_TRADE: allocator declines when any feasible action is unpriced
FEE_REGIMES: never pooled across the 2026-09-17T03:59Z cutover

ENTRIES.NAME: Proper scoring rules as the model-selection objective
ENTRIES.SOURCE: Gneiting & Raftery 2007 JASA 102(477) 359-378; Brier 1950 Mon. Wea. Rev.; Murphy 1973 J. Appl. Meteor. (reliability-resolution-uncertainty partition)
ENTRIES.BETTOR_APPLICABILITY: HIGH. Propriety is a property of the scoring rule, not of the market, so it transfers without a structural assumption.
ENTRIES.CURRENT_BETTOR_EQUIVALENT: NONE. position_state.fair_value_status is three-valued (NOT_IDENTIFIED / FV_VENUE_IMPLIED / FV_VALIDATED) but VALIDATED has no scoring definition behind it.
ENTRIES.PROPOSED_CHANGE: Define FV_VALIDATED as a scored state. Report Brier as primary with its Murphy partition (RELIABILITY / RESOLUTION / UNCERTAINTY) and log score as a companion. Never average the two into one number.
ENTRIES.WHY_BRIER_PRIMARY: The log score is unbounded below. On binary event contracts quoted near 0.01/0.99 a single confident miss dominates the sample mean and would make model ranking hostage to one settled market. Brier is bounded; the log score is reported beside it so tail overconfidence is still visible.
ENTRIES.DATA_REQUIRED: Resolved BETTOR forecasts with the forecast frozen before settlement and joined to the venue's own resolution.
ENTRIES.VALIDATION_METHOD: Walk-forward score against two benchmarks: the climatological base rate and the venue mid at decision time.

ENTRIES.NAME: Calibration intercept and slope in preference to ECE
ENTRIES.SOURCE: Cox 1958 calibration regression; Van Calster et al. 2019 J Clin Epidemiol (calibration hierarchy); Naeini et al. 2015 AAAI and Kumar et al. 2019 NeurIPS on ECE estimator bias
ENTRIES.EMPIRICAL_SUPPORT: STRONG. The ECE estimator is known to be biased and binning-dependent; intercept/slope are estimable with standard errors.
ENTRIES.BETTOR_APPLICABILITY: HIGH
ENTRIES.CURRENT_BETTOR_EQUIVALENT: NONE
ENTRIES.PROPOSED_CHANGE: Carry CALIBRATION_INTERCEPT and CALIBRATION_SLOPE with confidence intervals per segment, plus a reliability curve. ECE is computed as DIAGNOSTIC_ONLY and may never gate a promotion.
ENTRIES.DATA_REQUIRED: Same as S1-01.
ENTRIES.VALIDATION_METHOD: Out-of-sample intercept CI covering 0 and slope CI covering 1.

ENTRIES.NAME: Platt scaling as default recalibration, isotonic only above a sample floor
ENTRIES.SOURCE: Platt 1999; Zadrozny & Elkan 2002 KDD; Niculescu-Mizil & Caruana 2005 ICML
ENTRIES.EMPIRICAL_SUPPORT: STRONG. Niculescu-Mizil & Caruana report isotonic overfitting on small samples and Platt winning below roughly one thousand observations, with isotonic overtaking it above that.
ENTRIES.BETTOR_APPLICABILITY: HIGH, and the sample-size finding is the operative part: BETTOR's segments will be small for a long time.
ENTRIES.CURRENT_BETTOR_EQUIVALENT: NONE
ENTRIES.PROPOSED_CHANGE: Two-parameter logistic recalibration by default. Isotonic admitted for a segment only when that segment's own resolved count exceeds a preregistered floor AND isotonic beats logistic out-of-sample on Brier.
ENTRIES.DATA_REQUIRED: Resolved forecasts per segment.
ENTRIES.VALIDATION_METHOD: Nested walk-forward: recalibration fitted on the training fold only, scored on the held-out fold.

ENTRIES.NAME: Shin probabilities as a third de-vig method, selected per segment
ENTRIES.SOURCE: Shin 1991 Economic Journal; Shin 1993 Economic Journal; Strumbelj 2014 Int. J. Forecasting
ENTRIES.EMPIRICAL_SUPPORT: MODERATE_TO_STRONG_BUT_MARKET_SPECIFIC. Strumbelj finds Shin better calibrated than basic normalisation on football odds; the margin is not uniform across markets and does not transfer by assertion.
ENTRIES.BETTOR_APPLICABILITY: MEDIUM. Shin models an insider-trading share in a bookmaker's overround. A CLOB with no bookmaker does not have an overround in the same sense, so Shin applies to the EXTERNAL sportsbook prior, not to the PMUS book itself.
ENTRIES.CURRENT_BETTOR_EQUIVALENT: edge-engine/src/edge/fairvalue/devig.py implements multiplicative and power only, with a module-level note that the method choice should be graded per league in shadow.
ENTRIES.PROPOSED_CHANGE: Add Shin beside multiplicative and power. Select the method per (sport, league, market_type) by out-of-sample calibration score with hierarchical backoff to the parent segment. Never select a single global method.
ENTRIES.DATA_REQUIRED: External odds snapshots with resolution, per segment.
ENTRIES.VALIDATION_METHOD: Walk-forward Brier plus calibration slope per segment against the incumbent power de-vig.
ENTRIES.OVERFIT_RISK: MEDIUM. Three methods times many segments is a selection surface; shrinkage and a multiple-testing control are required.

ENTRIES.NAME: Favourite-longshot bias is learned per segment, never applied as a formula
ENTRIES.SOURCE: Snowberg & Wolfers 2010 JPE; Wolfers & Zitzewitz 2004 JEP and 2006 on interpreting prediction-market prices
ENTRIES.EMPIRICAL_SUPPORT: STRONG_FOR_EXISTENCE_IN_RACETRACK_BETTING_WEAK_FOR_UNIVERSALITY. Snowberg & Wolfers find misperceptions fit better than risk-love. The sign is not universal: reverse bias is documented in several markets.
ENTRIES.BETTOR_APPLICABILITY: MEDIUM. The mechanism is a property of a market's participants, and PMUS participants are not racetrack bettors. Direction must be measured, not assumed.
ENTRIES.CURRENT_BETTOR_EQUIVALENT: The edge-engine measures edge by price band empirically (calib_price.csv, generated band config) which is the right shape already; there is no FLB correction applied anywhere, which is correct.
ENTRIES.PROPOSED_CHANGE: Keep price-band segmentation. Do NOT add an FLB correction term. Let the per-band calibration map absorb whatever bias exists, with its sign measured rather than imposed.
ENTRIES.DATA_REQUIRED: Resolved forecasts by price band per segment.
ENTRIES.VALIDATION_METHOD: Per-band calibration intercept; test whether a monotone band effect survives out-of-sample.

ENTRIES.NAME: Hierarchical shrinkage as the segmentation backbone, replacing hard sample thresholds
ENTRIES.SOURCE: Efron & Morris 1975 JASA; Buhlmann credibility theory; Gelman & Hill hierarchical models
ENTRIES.BETTOR_APPLICABILITY: VERY_HIGH. This is the single highest-value structural import in the audit, because BETTOR's problem is many thin segments rather than one thick one.
ENTRIES.CURRENT_BETTOR_EQUIVALENT: position_state.posterior_weight, posterior_weight_precision and blended_lambda already implement credibility blending, but ONLY for the whale pairing lambda.
ENTRIES.PROPOSED_CHANGE: Promote the existing blending machinery to a general hierarchical backoff used by every segmented parameter: GLOBAL -> SPORT -> LEAGUE -> MARKET_TYPE -> PRICE_BAND -> TIME_TO_EVENT -> PREGAME_LIVE -> LIQUIDITY_REGIME. A thin segment shrinks towards its parent instead of being gated off by a hard n.
ENTRIES.DATA_REQUIRED: Any segmented estimate plus its sample count and variance.
ENTRIES.VALIDATION_METHOD: Out-of-sample score of the shrunk estimator against both the pooled parent and the unshrunk segment.
ENTRIES.OVERFIT_RISK: LOW. Shrinkage reduces it by construction.

ENTRIES.NAME: FV carries its own uncertainty, not only a point estimate
ENTRIES.SOURCE: Standard Bayesian posterior predictive practice; Gneiting & Raftery 2007 on distributional rather than point forecasts
ENTRIES.BETTOR_APPLICABILITY: VERY_HIGH. It is the missing input that keeps robust dominance switched off today.
ENTRIES.CURRENT_BETTOR_EQUIVALENT: position_state.ev_cell already accepts EV_LOWER_BOUND and EV_UPPER_BOUND, and robust_dominance is disabled by BOUND_METHODOLOGY_VALIDATED = False because nothing defensible produces those bounds.
ENTRIES.PROPOSED_CHANGE: Emit FV_MODEL_CALIBRATED together with FV_CALIBRATION_UNCERTAINTY as a posterior interval. This is the defensible source for the EV bounds ev_cell already has slots for, and is the route to turning robust dominance on.
ENTRIES.DATA_REQUIRED: Posterior or bootstrap distribution of the calibrated probability per segment.
ENTRIES.VALIDATION_METHOD: Interval coverage: the stated 80 percent interval must contain the realised frequency about 80 percent of the time out of sample.
ENTRIES.OVERFIT_RISK: MEDIUM. An under-wide interval is worse than none, because it would switch robust dominance on spuriously.

ENTRIES.NAME: Cross-market consensus by log-odds pooling with learned extremisation
ENTRIES.SOURCE: Bates & Granger 1969; Clemen 1989 Int. J. Forecasting review; Satopaa et al. 2014 IJF; Baron et al. 2014 Decision Analysis
ENTRIES.BETTOR_APPLICABILITY: MEDIUM_TO_HIGH. Linear averaging of probabilities is systematically under-confident; log-odds pooling and extremisation address it, but the extremisation coefficient is a fitted parameter and must be earned.
ENTRIES.CURRENT_BETTOR_EQUIVALENT: NONE
ENTRIES.PROPOSED_CHANGE: Where several independent priors exist for one contract, pool in log-odds space. Treat any extremisation coefficient as a fitted parameter under the anti-overfitting standard, defaulting to 1.0 (no extremisation).
ENTRIES.DATA_REQUIRED: Two or more genuinely independent priors on the same contract, plus resolution.
ENTRIES.VALIDATION_METHOD: Walk-forward Brier of the pool against the best single source and against the simple average.

ENTRIES.NAME: The venue's own price may not be used as the independent fair value
ENTRIES.SOURCE: Wolfers & Zitzewitz 2006 on when prediction-market prices equal probabilities
ENTRIES.EMPIRICAL_SUPPORT: STRONG_THEORETICAL. Prices equal mean beliefs only under specific utility and wealth-distribution conditions; in general they do not.
ENTRIES.BETTOR_APPLICABILITY: DIRECT
ENTRIES.CURRENT_BETTOR_EQUIVALENT: position_state.fair_value_status ALREADY returns FV_VENUE_IMPLIED and refuses to treat it as validated, with the tautology argument stated in the docstring.
ENTRIES.PROPOSED_CHANGE: NONE. This is already correct and is recorded here so that a later 'simplification' cannot remove it without contradicting a cited result.
ENTRIES.DATA_REQUIRED: NONE
ENTRIES.VALIDATION_METHOD: Existing test coverage on fair_value_status.

ENTRIES.NAME: Separate FV_SETTLEMENT from FV_EXECUTION_SHORT_HORIZON
ENTRIES.SOURCE: Structural argument; supported by the microstructure literature that short-horizon expected price differs from terminal value (Glosten & Milgrom 1985; Stoikov 2018)
ENTRIES.BETTOR_APPLICABILITY: HIGH_ARCHITECTURALLY. The two quantities enter different EV terms and conflating them is a category error regardless of how big the gap turns out to be.
ENTRIES.CURRENT_BETTOR_EQUIVALENT: ONE fair value. position_state.fair_value_status returns a single status used by every fair-value-dependent EV term.
ENTRIES.PROPOSED_CHANGE: Two named objects with independent status and uncertainty. FV_SETTLEMENT prices inventory held to resolution and the settlement branch of the exit decision. FV_EXECUTION_SHORT_HORIZON prices the markout, the close cost and the adverse-selection term. fair_value_dependent_ev takes which of the two a term requires.
ENTRIES.DATA_REQUIRED: For the gap to be MEASURED rather than merely represented: paired observations of short-horizon price change and eventual resolution.
ENTRIES.CAN_TEST_NOW: PARTIAL. The representation can be built and tested offline now; the size of the gap cannot be established without fills.
ENTRIES.VALIDATION_METHOD: Test the hypothesis FV_SETTLEMENT != FV_EXECUTION_SHORT_HORIZON per state; report NOT_IDENTIFIED until it is powered.

ENTRIES.NAME: Micro-price as a short-horizon execution-FV challenger
ENTRIES.SOURCE: Stoikov 2018 Quantitative Finance, The micro-price
ENTRIES.BETTOR_APPLICABILITY: UNPROVEN_ON_PMUS_AND_THERE_IS_A_SPECIFIC_REASON_FOR_DOUBT. The micro-price is a sub-tick adjustment to the mid. PMUS ticks are one cent on a price range of one dollar, so the adjustment is large relative to nothing and small relative to the tick over much of the range; it may quantise away. The complement book is also a second, redundant observation of the same event, which has no equity analogue.
ENTRIES.CURRENT_BETTOR_EQUIVALENT: NONE. book_metrics computes mids and markouts but no imbalance-adjusted price.
ENTRIES.PROPOSED_CHANGE: Implement as a shadow estimator only. It becomes authoritative only if it beats the plain mid at predicting the realised mid at a native horizon, on BETTOR's own captures.
ENTRIES.DATA_REQUIRED: Top-of-book sizes plus forward mid at the horizon. BETTOR'S SEALED TICK CAPTURES ALREADY CARRY BOTH.
ENTRIES.VALIDATION_METHOD: Out-of-sample mean squared error of predicted versus realised mid at 30 / 60 / 300 s against the plain mid benchmark, walk-forward by capture segment.

ENTRIES.NAME: Queue imbalance as a short-horizon predictor, testable on already-sealed data
ENTRIES.SOURCE: Cont & de Larrard 2013 SIAM J. Financial Math; Huang, Lehalle & Rosenbaum 2015 JASA
ENTRIES.BETTOR_APPLICABILITY: TESTABLE_TODAY. This is the one entry in the audit that needs no new data and no venue contact.
ENTRIES.CURRENT_BETTOR_EQUIVALENT: The tick rows carry top-5 ladders and displayed size; book_metrics already computes markouts at MARKOUT_HORIZONS_S = (30, 60, 300). Nothing joins imbalance to markout.
ENTRIES.PROPOSED_CHANGE: Compute QI = (bid_size - ask_size)/(bid_size + ask_size) per tick and regress the forward mid change on it at each existing horizon, per sport and price band, with shrinkage.
ENTRIES.DATA_REQUIRED: NONE BEYOND WHAT IS ALREADY SEALED.
ENTRIES.VALIDATION_METHOD: Walk-forward by capture segment; benchmark is a zero-slope null. Report the coefficient with a CI, not a p-value alone.
ENTRIES.OVERFIT_RISK: MEDIUM. Many segments times three horizons needs a multiple-testing control.

ENTRIES.NAME: Order-flow imbalance (OFI) in the Cont-Kukanov-Stoikov sense
ENTRIES.SOURCE: Cont, Kukanov & Stoikov 2014 J. Financial Econometrics, The price impact of order book events
ENTRIES.EMPIRICAL_SUPPORT: STRONG_IN_EQUITIES. Price impact is close to linear in OFI.
ENTRIES.BETTOR_APPLICABILITY: BLOCKED_BY_DATA_NOT_BY_THEORY.
ENTRIES.CURRENT_BETTOR_EQUIVALENT: NONE, and it cannot exist on current captures. OFI is built from ADD, CANCEL and TRADE events at the touch. BETTOR captures SNAPSHOTS. tick_semantics records SHARES_TRADED_RESET_SEMANTICS = NOT_IDENTIFIED and maker_fill refuses to derive anything positive from the aggregate delta.
ENTRIES.PROPOSED_CHANGE: Do not approximate OFI from snapshot differences. Record it as the specific capability an event-level feed would unlock, and leave it unbuilt until such a feed exists.
ENTRIES.DATA_REQUIRED: An event-level stream with add / cancel / trade and an aggressor flag.
ENTRIES.VALIDATION_METHOD: NOT_IDENTIFIED until the feed exists.

ENTRIES.NAME: Inventory-adjusted reservation price, adapted to binary settlement
ENTRIES.SOURCE: Avellaneda & Stoikov 2008 Quantitative Finance 8(3) 217-224; Gueant, Lehalle & Fernandez-Tapia 2013 Math. Finan. Econ.
ENTRIES.BETTOR_APPLICABILITY: THE_PRINCIPLE_TRANSFERS_THE_COEFFICIENTS_DO_NOT. Three structural differences change the mathematics: (1) terminal value is 0 or 1, not a terminal mid, so per-contract terminal variance is p(1-p) rather than sigma^2 (T-t) and is MAXIMAL AT 50c and vanishing at the extremes; (2) the terminal time is real and known, which suits the AS finite-horizon structure better than an arbitrary equity session end; (3) the PMUS fee is theta*C*p*(1-p), so the venue already charges in proportion to the very quantity that measures binary inventory risk.
ENTRIES.CURRENT_BETTOR_EQUIVALENT: NONE. There is no reservation price. position_state chooses among discrete actions by EV comparison and declines when anything is unpriced.
ENTRIES.PROPOSED_CHANGE: Build AS_ADAPTED_CHALLENGER as a shadow quoting policy with a binary-specific reservation price r = FV_EXECUTION - q * gamma * V_binary * H, where V_binary is the exit-mode mixture of p(1-p) and path variance and H is the remaining exposure horizon. Half-spread comes from the fill-intensity model of S4-01, never from an assumed k.
ENTRIES.DATA_REQUIRED: gamma (a risk-preference choice, declared not fitted), the fill-intensity model, and a realised markout model.
ENTRIES.VALIDATION_METHOD: Shadow quoting compared with the incumbent discrete-action allocator on identical states, scored on counterfactual EV with the whole uncertainty carried through. It may not become authoritative on a paper argument.

ENTRIES.NAME: Transplanting Avellaneda-Stoikov numeric coefficients from equities
ENTRIES.SOURCE: Avellaneda & Stoikov 2008 and its many uncritical reimplementations
ENTRIES.BETTOR_APPLICABILITY: NONE
ENTRIES.CURRENT_BETTOR_EQUIVALENT: NONE, correctly.
ENTRIES.PROPOSED_CHANGE: Explicitly rejected and named, so that building S3-01 cannot quietly import k and gamma from a paper.
ENTRIES.DATA_REQUIRED: NOT_APPLICABLE
ENTRIES.VALIDATION_METHOD: NOT_APPLICABLE

ENTRIES.NAME: Bounded inventory with a hard maximum
ENTRIES.SOURCE: Gueant, Lehalle & Fernandez-Tapia 2013 (inventory bounds admit closed-form approximations)
ENTRIES.BETTOR_APPLICABILITY: HIGH_AND_ALREADY_PARTLY_PRESENT
ENTRIES.CURRENT_BETTOR_EQUIVALENT: The live mirror already enforces a per-order clip and a per-game cap; research/beta48 has event identity so a per-EVENT cap is expressible.
ENTRIES.PROPOSED_CHANGE: Express MAX_INVENTORY per EVENT rather than per market, using event_identity.index_events, because 1,557 contest markets collapse to 87 contests and per-market caps understate correlated exposure by roughly that ratio.
ENTRIES.DATA_REQUIRED: NONE. event_identity already produces the mapping.
ENTRIES.VALIDATION_METHOD: Recompute historical exposure under per-market versus per-event caps and report the difference.

ENTRIES.NAME: State-dependent fill hazard as a competing-risks survival model
ENTRIES.SOURCE: Cox 1972 proportional hazards; Fine & Gray 1999 JASA subdistribution hazard; Huang, Lehalle & Rosenbaum 2015 queue-reactive model
ENTRIES.BETTOR_APPLICABILITY: HIGH. The competing-risks framing is the important part and is usually got wrong.
ENTRIES.CURRENT_BETTOR_EQUIVALENT: NO_MODEL_AT_ALL, deliberately. book_metrics.FORBIDDEN_RENAMES already forbids calling a book quantity a FILL_RATE, and move_through_fill_probability raises MoveThroughIsNotAFill. BETTOR therefore does not currently have the single global passive fill rate that must be avoided.
ENTRIES.PROPOSED_CHANGE: Model P_FILL(horizon | state) as a COMPETING-RISKS problem over terminal events {FILLED, CANCELLED_BY_US, MOVED_AWAY_UNFILLED, EXPIRED} with STILL_RESTING right-censored. Treating cancel or move-away as plain censoring rather than as a competing event biases the fill probability upward, which is the error that flatters a maker strategy.
ENTRIES.DATA_REQUIRED: Our own resting-order lifecycles with placement, amendment, cancel and fill timestamps and the book state at each. THE LIVE MIRROR ALREADY PRODUCES THIS as a by-product of maker-first operation.
ENTRIES.CAN_TEST_NOW: PARTIAL. The estimator and its censoring tests can be built and unit-tested offline now; fitting needs the mirror's order lifecycles.
ENTRIES.VALIDATION_METHOD: Time-split concordance and calibration of predicted versus realised fill frequency by state bucket; benchmark is a single pooled fill rate, which the state model must beat out of sample.
ENTRIES.OVERFIT_RISK: HIGH. The state vector is wide and the event count will be small at first; shrinkage and a preregistered state list are required.

ENTRIES.NAME: Inferring fills from touch or aggregate traded volume
ENTRIES.SOURCE: Common practitioner shortcut; no defensible published basis for snapshot data
ENTRIES.BETTOR_APPLICABILITY: NONE
ENTRIES.CURRENT_BETTOR_EQUIVALENT: Already refused in three places: maker_fill has no branch returning a positive fill from ticks, book_metrics raises MoveThroughIsNotAFill, and tick_semantics keeps SHARES_TRADED_DELTA_STATUS = CONSERVATIVE_DIAGNOSTIC_ONLY.
ENTRIES.PROPOSED_CHANGE: NONE. Recorded so the fill-hazard build cannot reintroduce it as a convenience.
ENTRIES.DATA_REQUIRED: NOT_APPLICABLE
ENTRIES.VALIDATION_METHOD: Existing tests.

ENTRIES.NAME: Expected markout after fill, conditional on the fill
ENTRIES.SOURCE: Glosten & Milgrom 1985 JFE; standard markout practice in the microstructure literature
ENTRIES.EMPIRICAL_SUPPORT: STRONG. Adverse selection in quoted spreads is one of the most robust findings in microstructure.
ENTRIES.BETTOR_APPLICABILITY: HIGH. Any venue with informed flow has it; a sports event with in-play information has it by construction.
ENTRIES.CURRENT_BETTOR_EQUIVALENT: book_metrics computes markouts at (30, 60, 300) s as a DIAGNOSTIC over book state. Nothing conditions a markout on a fill, because there are no fills.
ENTRIES.PROPOSED_CHANGE: Define EXPECTED_MARKOUT_AFTER_FILL(state, horizon), signed against OUR side, and make it a required term of maker EV. The conditioning matters more than the horizon: E[markout | FILLED, state] is not E[markout | state], because we fill precisely when the other side wanted to trade.
ENTRIES.DATA_REQUIRED: Our own fills with the book state at fill and the mid at each horizon afterwards.
ENTRIES.VALIDATION_METHOD: Report the markout distribution by state bucket with CIs; the null to beat is zero markout.

ENTRIES.NAME: Markout horizons below the capture cadence
ENTRIES.SOURCE: Derivation from BETTOR's own capture design
ENTRIES.BETTOR_APPLICABILITY: CONSTRAINT_NOT_TECHNIQUE
ENTRIES.CURRENT_BETTOR_EQUIVALENT: MARKOUT_HORIZONS_S = (30, 60, 300).
ENTRIES.PROPOSED_CHANGE: A 5 s markout is not estimable from a 2.5 s grid with any precision and is not estimable at all from slower captures. Add short horizons only when a capture cadence supports them; until then report them NOT_IDENTIFIED rather than interpolating.
ENTRIES.DATA_REQUIRED: A faster capture, which is a separate rate-budget decision and is out of scope here.
ENTRIES.VALIDATION_METHOD: NOT_APPLICABLE

ENTRIES.NAME: VPIN as a toxicity measure
ENTRIES.SOURCE: Easley, Lopez de Prado & O'Hara 2012 RFS; critiqued by Andersen & Bondarenko 2014
ENTRIES.EMPIRICAL_SUPPORT: DISPUTED. The critique argues VPIN's predictive content is largely a mechanical function of volatility and volume bucketing.
ENTRIES.BETTOR_APPLICABILITY: LOW. It also needs trade classification BETTOR cannot perform without an aggressor flag.
ENTRIES.CURRENT_BETTOR_EQUIVALENT: NONE
ENTRIES.PROPOSED_CHANGE: Do not build. If an event feed ever arrives, VPIN may be computed as a diagnostic only and may never enter an EV term.
ENTRIES.DATA_REQUIRED: Classified trade flow.
ENTRIES.VALIDATION_METHOD: NOT_APPLICABLE

ENTRIES.NAME: Corrected EV_MAKER: risk terms live inside the fill branch
ENTRIES.SOURCE: Derivation from the law of total expectation; the error class is standard in applied EV work
ENTRIES.BETTOR_APPLICABILITY: DIRECT_AND_IMMEDIATE
ENTRIES.CURRENT_BETTOR_EQUIVALENT: position_state.ev_pair_now sums LOCKED_PAIR_VALUE, EXECUTION_COSTS, MAKER_REBATE, VERIFIED_INCENTIVES, INCREMENTAL_RISK and CAPITAL_RECYCLING_VALUE UNCONDITIONALLY. ev_wait does branch on p_complete and is the correct shape already.
ENTRIES.PROPOSED_CHANGE: EV_MAKER = P_FILL(h|s) * ( SPREAD_CAPTURE + MAKER_REBATE + VERIFIED_INCENTIVES - E[ADVERSE_MARKOUT | FILL,s] - E[INVENTORY_HOLDING_COST | FILL,s] - E[CLOSE_COST | FILL,s] ) + (1 - P_FILL) * 0 - CAPITAL_RESERVATION_COST(rest duration). Every risk term is CONDITIONAL ON THE FILL and sits inside the first branch. Subtracting adverse selection or inventory risk outside the branch double counts, because neither is incurred when the quote does not fill.
DOUBLE_COUNTING_FIXED: ADVERSE_SELECTION subtracted outside the fill branch while CONDITIONAL_VALUE_IF_FILLED is already net of it
OPPORTUNITY_COST subtracted separately while VALUE_IF_NOT_FILLED is also set to the value of the alternative use of capital
INVENTORY_RISK charged on an unfilled quote
ENTRIES.VALUE_IF_NOT_FILLED: Zero for the quote itself: no fill means no position and no inventory. The only genuine residual is the cost of any capital or quote slot reserved while resting, which is charged ONCE, outside the branches, as CAPITAL_RESERVATION_COST.
ENTRIES.DATA_REQUIRED: P_FILL from S4-01 and the conditional markout from S5-01; the formulation itself requires none.
ENTRIES.VALIDATION_METHOD: Unit tests that the identity holds and that a NOT_IDENTIFIED term in either branch propagates, per the existing ev_sum rule.

ENTRIES.NAME: EV_TAKER with size-bounded certainty of execution
ENTRIES.SOURCE: Derivation; consistent with the existing treatment of the aggressive close
ENTRIES.BETTOR_APPLICABILITY: DIRECT
ENTRIES.CURRENT_BETTOR_EQUIVALENT: inventory.py already treats the AGGRESSIVE close as identified only for as much size as the captured ladder displays, and NOT_IDENTIFIED beyond it. That is exactly the right rule and should be reused for entry.
ENTRIES.PROPOSED_CHANGE: EV_TAKER = (FV - ask) * size - TAKER_FEE(size, p, regime, tier) - E[INVENTORY_HOLDING_COST] - E[CLOSE_COST] + VERIFIED_INCENTIVES, with P_FILL = 1 ONLY up to displayed size at the crossed levels and NOT_IDENTIFIED beyond. Which FV enters depends on the intended exit: FV_SETTLEMENT for a hold-to-resolution intent, FV_EXECUTION_SHORT_HORIZON for an intent to close early.
ENTRIES.DATA_REQUIRED: Fee regime and tier, which fees_v2 already carries with TIER_VERIFIED = False.
ENTRIES.VALIDATION_METHOD: Unit tests on the size boundary and on regime straddles.

ENTRIES.NAME: EV_NO_TRADE as the declared numeraire
ENTRIES.SOURCE: Derivation
ENTRIES.BETTOR_APPLICABILITY: DIRECT
ENTRIES.CURRENT_BETTOR_EQUIVALENT: A_WAIT and A_NO_ACTION_RECORDED exist as actions; the numeraire convention is not stated anywhere.
ENTRIES.PROPOSED_CHANGE: Declare EV_NO_TRADE = 0 BY CONSTRUCTION and state that every other EV is measured relative to not trading. This is not a trivial line: without it, an opportunity-cost term gets added to the trading side AND the no-trade side is given a positive continuation value, which double counts the same quantity in opposite directions and biases the engine towards inaction or action depending on which side got it.
ENTRIES.DATA_REQUIRED: NONE
ENTRIES.VALIDATION_METHOD: A test asserting no EV term named opportunity or continuation appears on both sides of the comparison.

ENTRIES.NAME: Settlement is a guaranteed zero-spread exit with a known date
ENTRIES.SOURCE: Derivation from binary contract structure; contrast with Almgren & Chriss 2000 where no such terminal exit exists
ENTRIES.BETTOR_APPLICABILITY: VERY_HIGH_AND_UNDER_EXPLOITED
ENTRIES.CURRENT_BETTOR_EQUIVALENT: A_SETTLEMENT_HOLD exists as an action; inventory.py measures SETTLEMENT_OUTCOME and CAPITAL_OCCUPANCY in dollar-seconds.
ENTRIES.PROPOSED_CHANGE: Make SETTLE the explicit baseline that every other exit must beat. On a binary contract, holding to resolution costs no spread and no taker fee and terminates with certainty at a known date; its only costs are capital occupancy and the binary variance p(1-p). An aggressive close must therefore clear a HIGH bar, not a low one. This inverts the usual equity intuition that flat is free.
ENTRIES.DATA_REQUIRED: Capital opportunity rate, which is an allocation input rather than a market observation.
ENTRIES.VALIDATION_METHOD: Retrospective comparison of realised aggressive closes against the settlement counterfactual on the same inventory.

ENTRIES.NAME: Passive-to-aggressive conversion as optimal stopping with a deadline
ENTRIES.SOURCE: Optimal stopping theory; Gueant et al. inventory-liquidation variants
ENTRIES.BETTOR_APPLICABILITY: MEDIUM_ARCHITECTURALLY_LOW_NUMERICALLY
ENTRIES.CURRENT_BETTOR_EQUIVALENT: TIME_UNPAIRED_BUCKETS with whale-derived lambdas, and FRESH_SECONDS = 60. The bucket grid is frozen to match the prior and is explicitly never interpolated.
ENTRIES.PROPOSED_CHANGE: Keep the frozen bucket grid. Replace any implicit fixed age threshold with a comparison of EV_PASSIVE_CONTINUE against EV_AGGRESSIVE_NOW and EV_SETTLE at each tick, so the conversion time is an OUTPUT rather than a parameter.
ENTRIES.DATA_REQUIRED: The fill hazard and the close-cost model.
ENTRIES.VALIDATION_METHOD: Counterfactual comparison against the fixed-threshold incumbent on identical inventory paths.

ENTRIES.NAME: Almgren-Chriss optimal liquidation scheduling
ENTRIES.SOURCE: Almgren & Chriss 2000 Journal of Risk; Bertsimas & Lo 1998
ENTRIES.BETTOR_APPLICABILITY: LOW. The framework prices the trade-off between market impact and timing risk for an order large relative to displayed liquidity, over a horizon with no natural terminal payoff. BETTOR's clips are small relative to the book, and the contract self-liquidates at settlement. The binding constraint is adverse selection on a single clip, not impact from scheduling many.
ENTRIES.CURRENT_BETTOR_EQUIVALENT: NONE
ENTRIES.PROPOSED_CHANGE: Do not build. Revisit only if BETTOR's clip ever becomes large relative to displayed depth, in which case the relevant term is the ladder walk that inventory.py already bounds.
ENTRIES.DATA_REQUIRED: NOT_APPLICABLE
ENTRIES.VALIDATION_METHOD: NOT_APPLICABLE

ENTRIES.NAME: Full Kelly
ENTRIES.SOURCE: Kelly 1956 Bell System Technical Journal; MacLean, Thorp & Ziemba 2011
ENTRIES.BETTOR_APPLICABILITY: REJECTED_ON_THREE_SPECIFIC_GROUNDS, not on taste: (1) Kelly assumes p is KNOWN; BETTOR estimates it, and the growth function is asymmetric so overbetting is far more damaging than underbetting, with growth reaching zero at twice the Kelly fraction; (2) the log-growth objective presumes many independent repetitions, which correlated same-event contracts violate; (3) it carries no drawdown constraint, and BETTOR operates under one.
ENTRIES.CURRENT_BETTOR_EQUIVALENT: NONE. Sizing today is a proportional mirror rule with a per-order clip and a per-game cap.
ENTRIES.PROPOSED_CHANGE: Explicitly rejected and named in code, so that a future sizing change cannot arrive at full Kelly by default.
ENTRIES.DATA_REQUIRED: NOT_APPLICABLE
ENTRIES.VALIDATION_METHOD: NOT_APPLICABLE

ENTRIES.NAME: Risk-constrained Kelly with an explicit drawdown constraint
ENTRIES.SOURCE: Busseti, Ryu & Boyd 2016, Risk-Constrained Kelly Gambling
ENTRIES.BETTOR_APPLICABILITY: HIGH. It is the right shape: keep the log-growth objective but add a constraint that the probability of hitting a drawdown level stays below a declared bound, which yields a fraction of full Kelly as an OUTPUT of a stated risk preference rather than an arbitrary one-half or one-quarter.
ENTRIES.CURRENT_BETTOR_EQUIVALENT: Hard caps only: per-order clip, per-game cap, and a loss stop that is currently switched off by owner order.
ENTRIES.PROPOSED_CHANGE: Adopt the FORM: maximise expected log growth subject to a declared drawdown probability bound. The drawdown bound is an owner decision, not a fitted parameter. Hard caps remain as an outer envelope, because a constraint that depends on an estimated p must never be the only thing between BETTOR and a large position.
ENTRIES.DATA_REQUIRED: Calibrated p with uncertainty, and the correlation structure from event identity.
ENTRIES.CAN_TEST_NOW: PARTIAL. The optimiser can be built and tested on synthetic inputs now.
ENTRIES.VALIDATION_METHOD: Simulation under the fitted uncertainty, reporting realised drawdown frequency against the declared bound.

ENTRIES.NAME: EDGE_LOWER_CONFIDENCE_BOUND sizing, so size falls to zero as uncertainty grows
ENTRIES.SOURCE: Derivation combining Kelly's sensitivity to estimated edge with standard interval estimation; same principle as conservative plug-in estimators
ENTRIES.BETTOR_APPLICABILITY: VERY_HIGH. This is the direct answer to whether sizing should go to zero as uncertainty about edge increases: yes, and this is the mechanism.
ENTRIES.CURRENT_BETTOR_EQUIVALENT: position_state.ev_cell already carries EV_LOWER_BOUND and robust_dominance already compares a floor against every other ceiling, but it is DISABLED because BOUND_METHODOLOGY_VALIDATED = False. The machinery exists; the defensible bound does not.
ENTRIES.PROPOSED_CHANGE: Size on EDGE_LCB = lower quantile of (FV_posterior - price) rather than on the point edge. Two consequences follow automatically and neither needs a threshold: a wide posterior shrinks the position smoothly towards zero, and a posterior whose lower quantile does not clear the price produces NO TRADE without any separate rule.
ENTRIES.DATA_REQUIRED: FV_CALIBRATION_UNCERTAINTY from S1-07.
ENTRIES.CAN_TEST_NOW: PARTIAL. The sizing function is testable on synthetic posteriors now.
ENTRIES.VALIDATION_METHOD: Out-of-sample growth and drawdown of LCB sizing against point-estimate sizing at matched average exposure.
ENTRIES.OVERFIT_RISK: LOW_TO_MEDIUM. The quantile level is a declared risk preference, not a fitted parameter, and must be preregistered.

ENTRIES.NAME: Correlation and event concentration as the allocation unit
ENTRIES.SOURCE: Simultaneous-bet Kelly with correlated outcomes; standard portfolio constraint practice
ENTRIES.BETTOR_APPLICABILITY: HIGH_AND_THE_INPUT_ALREADY_EXISTS
ENTRIES.CURRENT_BETTOR_EQUIVALENT: event_identity.py maps 1,557 contest markets to 87 contests and states EVENT_COUNT_IS_NOT_CAPITAL_CAPACITY = True. The live mirror caps per game.
ENTRIES.PROPOSED_CHANGE: Make the EVENT the allocation unit everywhere, using the existing identity index, and treat markets within an event as one correlated exposure. Contracts on the same contest are not independent bets and sizing them as if they were overstates diversification by roughly the 1,557-to-87 ratio.
ENTRIES.DATA_REQUIRED: NONE BEYOND THE EXISTING INDEX.
ENTRIES.VALIDATION_METHOD: Recompute realised exposure per event versus per market on historical positions.

ENTRIES.NAME: Walk-forward temporal validation with purging and embargo
ENTRIES.SOURCE: Standard time-series practice; purging and embargo per Lopez de Prado 2018 (practitioner text, cited for the technique not as authority)
ENTRIES.BETTOR_APPLICABILITY: DIRECT. Sports contracts have long-lived overlapping labels, so a random split leaks.
ENTRIES.CURRENT_BETTOR_EQUIVALENT: NONE for model selection. The programme does have preregistration discipline (ENGINE_B_PREREGISTRATION, PRIOR_3 frozen with PRIOR_4 as a recorded ghost) which is the same instinct applied to priors.
ENTRIES.PROPOSED_CHANGE: All model selection by walk-forward splits, with labels purged across the settlement horizon and an embargo after each training fold. Random k-fold is forbidden by name.
ENTRIES.DATA_REQUIRED: Timestamped forecasts and resolutions.
ENTRIES.VALIDATION_METHOD: The method itself.

ENTRIES.NAME: Five separated metrics, never one headline number
ENTRIES.SOURCE: Murphy 1973 decomposition; Leitch & Tanner 1991 AER; Granger & Pesaran 2000 on decision-based forecast evaluation
ENTRIES.EMPIRICAL_SUPPORT: STRONG. Leitch & Tanner found conventional error measures correlate poorly with profits, which cuts BOTH ways: a profitable model need not be accurate, and an accurate model need not be profitable.
ENTRIES.BETTOR_APPLICABILITY: DIRECT
ENTRIES.CURRENT_BETTOR_EQUIVALENT: Partially present and genuinely good: position_state.incentive_split already separates TRADING_NET_EX_INCENTIVES from incentive P&L and stamps INCENTIVE_DEPENDENT; the architecture doc already mandates separate DIRECTIONAL_ENTRY_PNL / PAIR_COMPLETION_PNL / RESIDUAL_INVENTORY_PNL / EXIT_PNL ledgers.
ENTRIES.PROPOSED_CHANGE: Complete the set and report all five side by side: PROBABILITY_MODEL_QUALITY, TRADING_EDGE_BEFORE_EXECUTION, EXECUTION_QUALITY, INCENTIVE_PNL, TOTAL_REALIZED_PNL. A model may be rejected on weak statistical evidence even when TOTAL_REALIZED_PNL is positive, and that rejection must be expressible.
ENTRIES.DATA_REQUIRED: Decision-time snapshots joined to fills and resolutions.
ENTRIES.VALIDATION_METHOD: Each metric has its own benchmark; no metric substitutes for another.

ENTRIES.NAME: Multiple-testing control across model variants and segments
ENTRIES.SOURCE: White 2000 Econometrica, A Reality Check for Data Snooping; Hansen 2005 JBES, Superior Predictive Ability; Romano-Wolf stepdown
ENTRIES.BETTOR_APPLICABILITY: HIGH. This audit alone proposes several challengers across many segments; without a control, one of them will look significant by construction.
ENTRIES.CURRENT_BETTOR_EQUIVALENT: NONE
ENTRIES.PROPOSED_CHANGE: Any challenger promoted out of a family of variants must clear a White or Hansen-family test against the incumbent, with the full family declared BEFORE the comparison, not after.
ENTRIES.DATA_REQUIRED: The full set of candidate variants and their out-of-sample scores.
ENTRIES.VALIDATION_METHOD: The test itself.

ENTRIES.NAME: Selecting models on in-sample P&L
ENTRIES.SOURCE: The failure mode the whole stream exists to prevent
ENTRIES.BETTOR_APPLICABILITY: NONE
ENTRIES.CURRENT_BETTOR_EQUIVALENT: Not currently done.
ENTRIES.PROPOSED_CHANGE: Forbidden by name, so that a promising backtest cannot become a promotion.
ENTRIES.DATA_REQUIRED: NOT_APPLICABLE
ENTRIES.VALIDATION_METHOD: NOT_APPLICABLE
